text: On the Dretske-Tooley-Armstrong (DTA) account, the lawhood of 'all Fs are Gs' consists in what?
choices: The generalization's earning a place as an axiom or theorem in the deductive system that best balances simplicity and strength.
The essential dispositional nature of F, which constitutively includes producing G.
A second-order necessitation relation N holding between the universals F and G, from which the first-order regularity follows.
The mere truth of the universal generalization, provided it is expressed in purely qualitative predicates.
explanation: The DTA view makes lawhood a higher-order fact, a necessitation relation N(F,G) between universals that is ontologically additional to, and entails, the first-order regularity. Option 0 is Lewis's Best System Analysis, option 1 is Bird's dispositional essentialism, and option 3 is the naive regularity theory; DTA is defined precisely by positing N over and above any regularity.
